html:
The Spokane are an Interior Salish people of the Spokane River valley in what is now eastern Washington. Their name is usually translated "children of the sun".

They lived in bands along the river and its streams, fishing for salmon at the falls, digging camas and other roots, and hunting game. After horses reached the Plateau in the 1700s, some went east to hunt bison.

The fur trade came early: in 1810 David Thompson of the North West Company set up Spokane House, the first lasting trading post in the region. As settlers and miners arrived, the Spokane joined the war of 1858 against the US Army, alongside the Coeur d'Alene, Palouse and others. The army defeated them and slaughtered hundreds of their horses. In 1881 the Spokane Reservation was set up north of the river, and the city of Spokane grew up at their old falls. Their neighbours included the Kalispel, Nez Perce and Yakama.
sum: The Spokane are an Interior Salish people of the Spokane River valley in what is now eastern Washington. Their name is usually translated "children of the sun".
